newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSIGHT - NZ dlr soft at nervous start to big week.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NZ dlr soft at nervous start to big week.

text.p: An unnerved New Zealand dollar dipped against the U.S. dollar in early Monday trade amid talk of softening signals likely to stem from Thursday's budget and Friday's monetary policy statement, but dealers predicted a bout of short-covering would keep it steady until Wednesday.

In an early drop, as the U.S. dollar made something of a charge after the G-7 meeting, the Kiwi dipped to US$0.6838/45, versus a Friday close nearer 0.6860, but dealers said this was likely to be the short-term floor.
"The bottom for the day is around 0.6835-40. The market is likely to see a bit of a short squeeze," one said.

Exporters might take advantage of the pressures on the kiwi to take some cover, the dealer noted, as the broader expectation is that most traders will be looking to go quite short before Thursday. He saw a short squeeze pushing kiwi up to 0.6880.

ASB Bank, in its latest economic report, said the prospect of a benign inflation outlook influencing the Reserve Bank's MPS medium term view could see an endorsement of either current monetary condition levels, or even easier ones.
"Either projection is expected to lead to lower interest rates and lower exchange rates over the coming weeks," it said.
As for the budget, the combination of technical pressures on the fiscal path and a higher-than-expected borrowing need could also combine to slow the pace of public debt reduction.
"These sort of concerns do not normally encourage foreign investment," ASB noted.
The Trade Weighted Index notched down to 67.33 from 67.40 late on Friday.
